reviews.text: Joel Coen's adaptation pushes the mythic parameters of the story, turning it into an existential thriller of strange and potent beauty.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: A hardened neo-noir from a time before noir had a name. It’s a story of self-made losers striking at glory, but who, through hubris and self-doubt, are unable to hold on to it.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: A haunting scene in a beautifully haunted film....
reviews.author: Zach Youngs

reviews.text: Coen’s direction at times puts you into a mesmerizing gaze that never lets up. Denzel should be in contention for Best Actor but overall I’m not a #Shakespeare fan & was hoping for something a little more unique
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: The film’s neat, sleek facade takes away the passion and sadly comes off as calculated, contained, and lacking in grandeur. A technical marvel and acting showcase, The Tragedy of Macbeth adds nothing new to this famous tale.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: In The Tragedy of Macbeth, Coen's expertise allows him to paint a threatening world with an inspired and confident brush.
reviews.author: Kent M. Wilhelm

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is a mesmerizing technical masterpiece that could have benefited from a distinct take on the well-known Shakespearean tale.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Washington and McDormand bring a dramatic interpretation of the tragic tale. When the two actors are on screen, not a moment is wasted.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: It grabs a hold of you by the collar and keeps you focused through Bruno Delbonnel’s dark cinematography and performances that feel it’s straight from the horse’s mouth of great Shakespearean interpreters like Olivier and Branagh.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: The movie completely loses whatever energy it had to begin with when McDormand exits, because she was bringing the thrust and momentum of pure anger to the drama.
reviews.author: Robert Koehler

reviews.text: Denzel Washington gives a thunderous performance in Joel Coen’s stamp on Shakespeare.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Artistically, The Tragedy of Macbeth is a near-flawless piece of filmmaking, and it's additionally powered by a pair towering turns from Denzel Washington and Frances McDormand.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: The elder Coen brings his proven visual and screenwriting know-how to some well-traveled material, joining two Oscar winners to put a new spin on a timeless Shakespeare’s tragedy. The results are wickedly satisfying.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Something astonishing this way comes... another masterwork full of sound and fury signifying everything.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text:
The Tragedy of Macbeth is great. The film has stunning cinematography, immersive production design, and strong performances from both Washington and McDormand.

Coen delivered on a visually unique adaption of Shakespeare’s work.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: A strange film in the best sense, it's daring, and it captures Shakespeare's spirit, that man who knew everything about human nature...  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: The way Joel Coen was able to combine a stage play and cinematic experience is unlike anything I've seen.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text:
A film whose sole purpose is to instill doubt in all things.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Shapes the exploration of the vicissitudes of ambition that takes shape in cruelty: the sweet taste of power, which is ephemeral, and the bitterness of accessing it through crime.
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: The world of The Tragedy of Macbeth is a stark one, colored in with shadows. Its hermetic and stage-y  a strength, I think. Here we see how the bounds of Shakespeare, film, and acting swell to tell such a story.
reviews.author: Zosha Millman

reviews.text: When the best thing in a Coen film is a long sword fight, something is missing, and The Tragedy of Macbeth is a movie where we can pinpoint what it was.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: It fits right in with the new anti-art orthodoxy. It’s as if Coen -- and how many others? -- were afraid to truly touch our imagination.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: While Washington has the gravitas to make Macbeth’s moments of fury truly unsettling, his performance is also nuanced enough to make the king seem petty, petulant, small.
reviews.author: Paul Thompson

reviews.text: Dang this was good. Expressionist, tilting the story far into genre horror...
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: The sparseness and symbolism of Coen’s film brings the illusory nature of power into even sharper focus.
reviews.author: Erin Schwartz

reviews.text: Its a gorgeous work of art, retaining the Coens dark sensibilities while taking rewarding chances.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: "The name Shakespeare invokes a scholarly lens, and if Coen has accomplished one thing with the pure mood of his take, its discovering a deliciously eerie new vehicle for one of the poets most lasting works."
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: Joel Coens film is brilliant. Its minimalistic approach balanced with powerhouse performances, infectious production design, and enchanting cinematography leads to one of Shakespeares finest adaptations.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Director Joel Coen screws his courage to the sticking-place and delivers  without the aid of his brother, Ethan, for the first time in his career  a movie that is as starkly ambitious and  brutally effective as the title character himself.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth features an absurdly talented ensemble working on a project that doesn't have much of a reason to exist.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: With an exceptional eye for its craftwork and technical elements and how those benefit the narrative, The Tragedy of Macbeth offers an enriching and captivating experience.
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: With digitization being the modern stage, Coen's film embraces the format. But this critic felt consumed by many of the visual choices and distanced by the storytelling, which is a shame, given the film's monumental performances.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Everyone exists in this ominous otherworld that feels so appropriate for characters who are caught between film and theater, ambition and loyalty, insanity and sanity, humanity and inhumanity.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: The film arguably does little that Welles didn't do in 1948 under the parsimonious oversight of Republic Pictures; but why argue with a new opportunity to experience the unbeatable combination of cinematic expressionism and Shakespearean expression?
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: With a Macbeth that is as technically meticulous as he is powerful, Denzel Washington once again makes the argument that he is our greatest living actor.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Macbeth is one of Shakespeare's shortest, most propulsive plays, something at its core seems to refuse being captured on film. Consider this a good, striking attempt.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: It's not exactly cheerful holiday viewing, but this "Macbeth" is nonetheless a gift.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Stands out from other Shakespeare adaptations with two towering central performances, a singularly foreboding vibe and incredible production design that is sure to garner Academy Award consideration.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: The film has a cold, abstract beauty.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Every beat of "The Tragedy Of Macbeth" a cinematic flourish, a tale told by a master full of sound and monochrome fury.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: The over-all effect is of a striving toward a high style that isn't achieved-and that undercuts the mighty import of the play.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Coen has created a cinematic masterpiece from a Shakespeare masterpiece.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: To mangle a famous line in the play for a halfwit critic's quotes sake ... "By the pricking of my thumbs, something excellent this way comes." Eerie/magnificent light & magic.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is Joel Coen's first film without his brother Ethan. And the movie isn't just a triumph - it's a reminder that, even with the dismal state of cinema today, movies can still surprise us.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: Shot in haunting black-and-white, The Tragedy of Macbeth begins slowly, even hesitantly, but steadily accrues power as it goes along.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Fine performances and striking visuals with an angular, expressionistic zeal can't help but make this feel like anything other than an academic exercise.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: [O]ne of the starkest, strangest and saddest new films you're likely to encounter. Possessed of a stunning throwback aesthetic and driven by phenomenal performances, it's unlike anything I've seen in ages.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: [Coen] blends naturalistic performances with startling set pieces.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: An exceptional style exercise in which theater and cinema converge under the overwhelming strength of its performances and the hypnotic power of Bruno Delbonnel's monochrome cinematography.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Joel Coen puts a fine point on defining traitors as those "who swear a lie." You know who you are.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: You feel like an audience member fully immersed in the unraveling of fate's odious design.
reviews.author: Princess Weekes

reviews.text: It adapts the Shakespearean tragedy with a solemn and atmospheric monochrome style that never loses its aesthetic horizon illustrated in black and white. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: If Macbeth comes across as self-consciously arty and occasionally juiceless it is because it lacks the initiative to transform, rather than simply render, the material.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Bell

reviews.text: Getting through the Shakespearean style is still a bit of a sludge but this cast is first rate.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Love that Joel Coen diversified this classic tale as a master class in acting from Oscar winners Denzel Washington and Frances McDormand coupled with magnificent use of cinematic shadow imagery
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: I came away from it appreciating the craft but feeling a bit hollow.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Washington and McDormand are brilliant, as are the rest of the cast, handling the daunting task of taking such well-worn lines and restoring them once again as part of a whole from their cultural vernacular.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: To call The Tragedy of Macbeth 'fun' feels wrong, but it is, undoubtedly, imbued with a darkly comic sensibility.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Boiling Shakespeare's play down to its most elemental parts, Joel Cohen's Tragedy of Macbeth is an exercise in lavish, purposeful minimalism executed from a place of experience and taste.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: The movie, which was shot in black and white, is visually stunning in a way that greatly enhances the drama, and the actors wear period costumes, since updating it to the modern era is so 20th century.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: The low-key acting adds a human element to scenes that are often played as formalities.
reviews.author: Michael Wood

reviews.text: As you'd expect it is masterfully directed. However, it's Bruno Delbonnel's cinematography and Stefan Dechant's production design that really make this version of the Scottish Play leap from the screen.
reviews.author: Alan Corr

reviews.text: It's all a glorious reminder of the thrill movies can create [and] how they can inject life through real artistry ...
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: Eschewing the artifice of reality, Coen creates an experience that is Cathartic as well as horrifying, akin to the medieval morality plays or even the tragedies of classical Greece
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: I didn't get a five-star feeling from it. It was interesting, but Macbeth can't just be interesting.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Washington starts wise and quickly devolves into a fool, and the horror on Mcdormand’s face during his public slip-ups have a seriocomic touch. Kathryn Hunter leaves a strong impression as all of the witches.
reviews.author: Sankhayan Ghosh

reviews.text: One of the best Shakespearian adaptations in a generation.
reviews.author: Michael Medved

reviews.text: Joel Coen's The Tragedy of Macbeth is both satisfying and limited, spot-on and slightly off, for myriad reasons. But you can't fault it for lacking a genuine sense of interpretation.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: This is Coen, yes, but fundamentally this is Shakespeare. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is ultimately worth seeing in the end, though I suspect that, unlike the majority of [Joel Coen's] oeuvre, it is not one that many people will find it necessary to revisit too often in the future.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Inspired, audacious interpretation of one of Shakespeare's most compelling plays.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is bold, ferocious, gritty, and starkly beautiful. Something wicked this way comes, indeed.
reviews.author: Alex McPherson

reviews.text: Joel Coen's The Tragedy of Macbeth is every bit as bold as you'd expect a Joel Coen take on Shakespeare to be.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: At once an experiment and a retrenchment. After all, what is Shakespeare's tale but another of Coen's beloved noirs?
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It could just roll out its cast and reap the accolades. Coen makes this a memorable take with an actor's showcase presentation and striking visuals.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: It is a movie defined by its emptiness; the vacancy of its Brutalist hallways and the desolation of its deliberately artificial landscapes.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Squinting isn't necessary to see modern reflections in a delusional fascist ruler encouraged by prophetic messages to violently secure power. Witches cackling predictions about forests that walk wouldn't make a top 10 list of Most Bonkers QAnon Forecasts.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Washington and McDormand are ferocious as the ambitious Macbeths...
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: Joel Coen has made his Macbeths into real adults, who seem to drag real responsibilities behind them.
reviews.author: Jo Livingstone

reviews.text: ...though "stark" would definitely describe the production design, the dominant effect is one of stunning beauty.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Coen has not only surrounded his leads with steady, tempered performances - from Corey Hawkins as Macduff to Bertie Carvel as Banquo - but has directed both Washington and McDormand to take a wearier, more cool-headed approach.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: What lingers in the mind after this version of The Tragedy of Macbeth is not specific line deliveries or bravura acting moments-although the cast all acquit themselves well-but images and sounds.
reviews.author: Isaac Butler

reviews.text: This latest adaptation of the masterwork could dominate Oscar night as Denzel Washington, Frances McDormand and some supremely talented supporting players make waves. Washington breathes life into the title role and McDormand completes him.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: Both performances are excellent, making clear every choice and every point.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: ... retains the spirit of the source material while darkening the tone and sharpening the focus to exhilarating effect.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Presented entirely in black and white, the film features a claustrophobic, noir-ish style that feels like nothing so much as a horror movie.
reviews.author: Lacy Baugher

reviews.text: Not since Roman Polanski's adaptation has a film of the Scottish Play stared so deeply and rapturously into the ruins of human ambition. Coen does it with fidelity to the Folio, shrewd casting, and a few strategic interpretative landmines.
reviews.author: David Cote

reviews.text: In a time where movies feel increasingly manufactured off an assembly line, here is an entry meticulously fashioned by artists who know exactly what they're doing.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: The most sublime acting is from Kathryn Hunter, who plays all three witches. It's a unique creative choice to have one person tackle the trio of roles, and what Hunter magnificently delivers is shapeshifting genius.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: This version from director Joel Coen, however, leans into theatrical minimalism -- the colours have been bled out into monochrome, the locations are expressed in geometrically stark, barely there props, and every syllable is consciously articulated.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The best of [Coen's flourishes] is the portrayal of the witches who are consolidated into one human body brought to life by an impressive Kathryn Hunter.[Full Rev. in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: With the visuals of The Tragedy of Macbeth, Coen takes an empty canvas and applies just a few oblique blots of ink; the detail is still there-it just requires a different sort of concentration.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Joel Coen has himself a good bloody time with the Bard, and Denzel Washington goes wonderfully nuts.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: This is Shakespeare done impolitely, and unforgettably.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Masterfully done
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: With "Tragedy of Macbeth," something wicked this way comes -something familiar to anyone who remembers high school English classes but also at times a darkly enchanting delight.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: The sound and fury is provided by Kathryn Hunter, who gives life to the three fortune-tellers with whom Macbeth - and the viewer - will lose his mind. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Santiago Alverú

reviews.text: A staggering take on the classic tale.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: A hypnotic film... [It] takes the viewer to another dimension. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: An exquisite adaptation of the literary classic. Delbonnel's cinematography is a beauty, while production design and sound are amazing. Washington and McDormand give strong performances in this awards contender. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Stunning visuals can only go so far in distracting us from the fact that it's emotionally uninvolving. Washington does well in a role he's too old for, but is let down by screenplay issues. Hawkins and Hunter are stand-outs, but it's largely disappointing
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: Joel Coen's Tragedy of Macbeth is a triumph, from eerie start to its grisly finish.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: A film that is loyal to a fault. With only Shakespearean English spoken and shot in all black and white, it feels too pretentious for its own good.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: It's a streamlined version of Shakespeare's play - it's 105 minutes long - but Coen, who wrote the screenplay, maximizes the impact. You won't feel shortchanged. Dazzled, more like.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Something old and something new in glorious black and white, the filmed stage play strips visuals down to bare elements, shrouding irrelevance in billowing mists and pools of darkness... because somewhere, Tim Burton is surely smiling.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: At once wonderful and exasperating; a demented and beautiful delight shaped with risk-taking boldness and considerable maturation in the proceedings.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The central relationship being empty just really killed this film for me.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: If any of our listeners want to find out whether Shakespeare or the Earl of Oxford wrote the play, they would only have to open the grave and see who had turned over.
reviews.author: Charles Solomon

reviews.text: This gorgeously shot and designed. it is worth seeing just for the visuals... For the most part, the performances are excellent.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: You'd think this Shakespeare play would fit Joel Coen. No such luck, I'm afraid. One of Shakespeare's greatest plays turns out as below-average Coen.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: The morality of it all seems weightless. But, boy, is it something to look at.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: At once dignified and deranged, Denzel Washington's Macbeth is just one of countless pleasures to be found in The Tragedy of Macbeth, director Joel Coen's gorgeously austere adaptation of Shakespeare's spooky saga about power and madness.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: The emotionally energetic performances give the film several strong kicks.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Coen shows far greater interest in Shakespeare's language than his cinematic predecessors, and his accomplished cast speak Shakespeare's verse comfortably and naturally.
reviews.author: James Shapiro

reviews.text: Has there ever been a more visually ravishing Macbeth -- or any Shakespeare film, for that matter - than this new version of "the Scottish play" from Joel Coen?
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth exists because Coen knew exactly how to make it one of the best films of the year, and one of the best Shakespeare movies ever made.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: While Coen presents plenty that is worth celebrating, they never answer the questions that should inform an adaptation that's been done in countless forms: Why this? Why now?
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: These are two people that can think about power, and even their way to it, but lose their mind because they do not feel powerful. #diandrareviews
reviews.author: Diandra Reviews

reviews.text: It feels almost Shakespearian, meets Edgar Allen Poe...
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: We appreciate the uniqueness of this production and individuality of the performances by Washington and McDormand. Although this is not your classic expectation of Shakespeare, Coen presents a new way to envision the Bard.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Coen's keen eye and Bruno Delbonnel's jaw-dropping cinematography help transport us into a world that at once feels alien and timeless, bound to its theatrical roots and yet boldly cinematic.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Among modern directors, there may be none better to embrace the tale's murderous absurdities than Joel Coen. There also are few finer to embody its specifically and sloppily male assertion of fiefdom than an emeritus alpha like Denzel Washington.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Working for the first time without his brother Ethan, Coen's film adaptation, featuring Denzel Washington as Macbeth, embraces the text with unusual faithfulness.
reviews.author: Forrest Cardamenis

reviews.text: The film’s strength undoubtedly lies in Bruno Delbonnel’s stunning cinematography: sets are uncomfortably empty and cold, the image’s inky black and white is suitably visceral, and the claustrophobic framing locks the viewer in with the actors.
reviews.author: Laura Potier

reviews.text: Succeeds in recasting this material as surreal, psychological horror.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Coen has cut and condensed the play to a tight 105 minutes, shedding anything remotely extraneous, and focusing exclusively on the main storyline and most prominent characters.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Denzel Washington and Frances McDormand, already two of the most celebrated actors of our time, deliver career-highlight performances in Joel Coen's ethereal take on the Bard.
reviews.author: Samuel R. Murrian

reviews.text: Despite freakishly austere settings, Frances McDormand as the 'Lady' and one Coen brother (Joel) at the helm, there's never anything bloody simple about this 'Tragedy.' Naturally, Denzel Washington's work in the lead is to die for, too.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Visually striking and impeccably cast, The Tragedy of Macbeth is one of the best Shakespeare adaptations to be put to the screen.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: ...Washington captures the nobility of Macbeth, but not the hubris or the venality...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Fueled by its powerful performances and visceral stage-setting, The Tragedy of Macbeth succeeds in what it aims to do: tell the 400-year-old story with nuance, purpose and accessibility.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: The hypnotic quality of the filmmaking complements the rhythm of the language.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The austere visual aesthetics is absolutely stunning but it's no style-over-substance as the acting is a triumph. The film exceeds my expectations in every respect, Joel Coen imbues a fresh, modern take to the classic Shakespearean tale.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Something wicked this way comes in "The Tragedy of Macbeth" and it all works.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: McDormand similarly rips into Lady Macbeth with the zeal of someone who's always wondered how she'd handle the role. Turns out she's a natural.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: It is a visually searing tour de force from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: It emphasises brooding atmosphere, nuanced performances and, most importantly, the Bard's above average dialogue.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: I could see The Tragedy of Macbeth becoming a favorite Shakespearean film adaptation, for those who rank such things. Watching it, I felt as if I were part of the audience seeing the play for the first time, from the pit.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Joel Coen's first film not co-directed by his brother, Ethan, is as good as their collaborations, and superior to Orson Welles' 1948 Macbeth.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: Anchored by a riveting performance by Oscar-winner Denzel Washington, the traditional narrative is enhanced by Bruno Delbonnel's haunting black and white cinematography.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: This is a dense, ingenious, hermetically sealed marvel.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: A haunted interpretation of Shakespeare that underscores my belief that the Coen Brothers - in this case, just Joel - are/is among our finest literary critics.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Also adding to a rich atmosphere of portent and potency, Coen regular Carter Burwell's understated, haunting score is also a terrific example of this production's winning less-is-more approach.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: The way it moves, the way it looks, and the way it feels is otherworldly. Like you're dropped into the Twilight Zone in the 17th Century.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Shakespeare's text comes richly to life in this heartbreaking and vivid retelling.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: A purely absorbing experience, as it should be, and will continue to be as more artists will continue finding bloody meaning in its words.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Even so, don't resign yourself to seeing this one at home - for all the movie's faults, you can always trust a Coen to make the most of a big canvas.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Beautifully shot in heavy black and white, Coen's film moves towards its bloody climax with relentless purpose, and the director's version of medieval Scotland is grandly theatrical, deliberately so.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Stylistically Coen's film is full of contradictions. It's breathtakingly cinematic with wonderful use of light, shadow, and fog. Yet much of the action is shot on sets that feel distinctly theatrical in terms of being confined interior spaces.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: It's a grand reimagining and well acted, with a solid supporting cast, most notably Kathryn Hunter as the witches. As opulent and beguiling as it is to look at, there's something with the tempo and arc that feels a bit off.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: It's a Macbeth reliant instead on psychological darkness where longing and complacency are the real lurking spooks.
reviews.author: Jeva Lange

reviews.text: ...one of the most effective, spell-binding takes on the famous play ever committed to screen.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: A very impressive Shakespeare adaptation and one of the best of MACBETH. (Coen sort of outdoes Orson Welles at his own game here).
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: As striking as the staging is, the unfortunate reality, or should that be the tragedy, is that the film itself can only push its boundaries from a visual standpoint, with the script merely rehashing Shakespeare's words.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Coen ends up with something that is neither merely film nor theater, but a mutation of both, taking advantage of the wide berth of expressionism we allow work on the stage, as well as the tools (visual effects, shock edits, etc.) of the screen.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Contorting her body as though she has turned into a raven or changing her voice since she's possessed by multiple spirits, [Kathryn] Hunter becomes an enigmatic imp, and the film's best special effect.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: Whatever its shortfalls, this movie has two of the very best actors of their generation playing two of the greatest roles in Western drama. That's not something one should skip lightly.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: She appears infrequently in the film, also doing double as the old man who witnesses Banquo's death, yet Hunter steals the film and captivates with magnetic power.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: With some of the year's most exceptional visuals and two powerhouse performances, Joel Coen proves he can be just as impressive as a solo act.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: This is that rare film where the atmosphere always seems to match the tone of those in the scene...and it's that level of detail and aesthetic choices that make The Tragedy of Macbeth one of Coen's most harrowing works.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: All told, this version of Macbeth may very well be the finest film adaptation of the Bard since Kenneth Branagh's auspicious debut with HENRY V in 1989.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: A fearsome hallucination in stark black-and-white... less hyperreal than hyper-dreamt, relentlessly crisp.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: The energy in this Macbeth rarely feels shocking or challenging instead its staid presentation intimates sanctity and prestige with little nerve or emotion.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Stunning to behold as it may be, Joel Coen's The Tragedy of Macbeth threatens to unravel into farce in its manic dash to the finish.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: A recitation is all this version of Macbeth is. The soul is, sadly, long gone.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is a visually stunning and faithful Shakespearean adaptation fueled by captivating performances from its stars.
reviews.author: Chris Agar

reviews.text: A meticulously executed production with striking German and French expressionist sensibilities.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Masterful filmmaking mixes and matches the text with compelling images and wonderful performances to create a new take on the Scottish Play that is both respectful and fearlessly fresh.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The fact that Coen gives no new insights into this Shakespearean tale makes its existence sort of redundant and futile.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth strikes a skillful balance between its striking visual presentation and its presentation of the play.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: There is no shortness of acting brilliance or production value perfection in every corner and millisecond of this picture.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: This Macbeth is as much about mood as it is about verse. The visuals acknowledge this, pulling us into the action as if we were seeing it on stage.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: I got a faithfully constructed story but one without a soul. This is a problem.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: It's one of the most visually striking and leanest versions of "the Scottish play" ever put on film, with blockbuster performances from Oscar winners Frances McDormand and Denzel Washington as Lady and Lord Macbeth, and a brilliant supporting cast.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: In addition to being an extraordinarily poetic film noir, The Tragedy of Macbeth is a strong contender as finest horror movie of the year.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: [Denzel Washington] is in his best form.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: I admire 'The Tragedy of Macbeth,' even if it feels like the movie is holding me at arm's length.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Finding ways to creatively bring out the most from such a stark setup is clearly the challenge that's been accepted and then turned on its head.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: It's an always striking-looking film, even if its exquisitely mannered presentation partially drains the beating heart out of the Bard's shortest, most lethal play.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Scenes flow into one another with a swiftness and elegance that builds its own momentum. Rarely have these nightmarish events seemed more inevitable.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Coen plays riddles with the viewer, just as witches play guessing games with Macbeth.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: What Coen does here is so staged and otherworldly in its approach that it somehow makes you examine the work anew after all these centuries.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is a triumph. I hope Shakespeare and Coen can work together again some day.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: "The Tragedy of Macbeth" is a startling staging of a classic with a life and energy all its own.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: It's very uniquely done.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: With a face burning with muted rage and lust for power, Washington registers another compelling performance, his portrait of Macbeth a boiling cocktail of contradiction who, just like other Shakespearean leading men, just can't tell good advice from bad.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Coen is going for a radical form of defamiliarization, and it's a bold move.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Tragedy of Macbeth more than earns its existence. See it not to feel better about the world but to understand its horrors, its art, and its absurdity.
reviews.author: Colleen Morrissey

reviews.text: Coen does a wonderful job with a bizarre and unforgettable performance from Kathryn Hunter...
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: No matter how cursed or unlucky the so-called "Scottish play" is in theater lore, the stars seem to be aligned here.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: "The Tragedy of Macbeth," led with tantalizing scorn and reverence by the untouchable Denzel Washington, is a different type of Shakespearean beast.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Joel Coen takes a stab at Shakespeare's murderous Macbeth, creating a spare, subtle, version of Shakespeare's tale of murder and guilt.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: This cold telling of the enduring tale is more of a triumph of form over substance. It's hard to dismiss the clinical nature of the entire exercise that does little narratively to distinguish itself.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: It's clear that Joel Coen trusts the language and his actors to do the work as he doesn't try to overwork the piece by giving it an alternative timeline or design concept.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Rather than "sound and fury signifying nothing," Joel Coen's direction drips with symbolism in a directorial masterclass where every shot selection, every camera angle, every macabre nightmare sequence conveys deeper meanings.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: There is no comfort in Coen's vision, but his rigor - and Washington's vigor - are never less than exhilarating.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: What is served is a full meal, delicious from the first frame to last, with a helpful side of thespian performances.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: At every moment, there's something to look at and appreciate, and these visuals are always in the service of reinforcing an overall mood or feeling.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Sometimes a film just aggressively leaves one cold...while Bruno Delbonnel's silvery, misty, close-up cinematography is striking, all the German Expressionism on display renders this one "Lady Macbeth in the Cabinet of Dr. Caligari."
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: By the pricking of my thumbs, something wickedly entertaining this way comes.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Joel Coen's The Tragedy of Macbeth is an outstanding gem of form and content, and I take solace that future generations of English students now have a new text to learn from.
reviews.author: Josh Kupecki

reviews.text: The aesthetic is a perfect fit for the mood of dread and things askew.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: It's as though [Coen] planned everything out for Broadway to ensure the actors remained grounded before expanding his visual scope to cinematic heights.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: It's Washington who dominates, of course, and not just because Macbeth dominates the play. His presence is that commanding.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: The pursuit of power by any means necessary - and the moral injury that ensues - feels both ancient and urgently new, especially when it's animated by the artistry and acute intelligence on display here.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: What is the point, really, of Joel Coen doing a Shakespeare adaptation at this stage of his career? A wonderful-looking film that feels more like a filmmaker curating his legacy than striving for something compelling.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: An inspired, modern interpretation.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Striking and powerful, with Coen finding his own way with the feature, which emphasizes the madness and violence of the play, joined by a newfound level of claustrophobia.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: There are bold aesthetic choices that command attention - but when these offer more food for thought than Shakespeare's prose, then it's clear that the real tragedy of this Macbeth is just how disappointing it is.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: The promise of the combo: Coen, Washington, McDormand and, oh yeah, Shakespeare, may be scintillating, the result is every bit as stunning as we'd hoped.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: There's an overall sense of men trying to keep out a spectral presence they don't understand.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: The leads are terrific, but Coen's vision stands apart because of its unsettling atmosphere, which is spellbinding and seductive.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: This is a Macbeth for the head rather than the heart, but no less beguiling for that.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: This is all potent territory for Coen, directing for the first time without brother Ethan.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: It is a small, wicked wonder that it took this long for a Coen brother to make Macbeth.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is an interesting new visual interpretation of the classic play and worth a watch.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is a triumph of Coen. Come for the classic tale, or one of the most talented working filmmakers today making his first directorial solo effort, but stay for the magnificently maddening embodiment of Macbeth from Denzel Washington
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The black-and-white cinematography contributes to the general spotlessness, as well as defining a precise chiaroscuro nightmare, like a Murnau horror.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Though reverent to its references, it is an entirely singular, and overwhelmingly expressive, piece of art.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is a meticulously crafted, visually stunning, and well-acted Shakespeare adaptation.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Stark and severe, with a level of artistry rarely achieved in movies, this black-and-white tragedy may be the best Macbeth ever made, and it's certainly one of the best-ever Shakespeare adaptations.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: A simple but moderately effective adaptation, aesthetically and thematically existing somewhere between The 400 Blows and The Raven. However, one wishes it were a bit more inventive like the Coens' O Brother, Where Art Thou? was of Homer's The Odyssey.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Shakespeare's The Tragedy of Macbeth has never been visualized in such a creative way. Hollywood titans Denzel Washington and Frances McDormand lead a banner ensemble in the classic tale of bloody ambition.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: A very interesting hybrid of film and theater. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: This barebones style of storytelling leads to some noticeable issues in terms of context... Still, these issues are slim for this writer, and the minimalistic, yet altogether striking cinematography serves itself well for Coen's vision
reviews.author: Adonis Gonzalez

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is a masterpiece of incredible set design, fantastic lead performances, and giving the classic play that A24 horror sheen that makes all of their movies just a little unnerving.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Fog and mist, translucent pavilion sidewalls, blowing curtains, dark water, shadows, reflections: the film is full of motifs evoking the murkiness in which Macbeth's last days play out.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: Love or hate The Tragedy of Macbeth, there's no question it contributes something refreshing and new to an outdated genre.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: The powerhouse performances from Denzel Washington, Frances McDormand, and the stellar Kathryn Hunter make this a must-see cinematic experience.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Falls short of the nightmarish power of Welles or Polanski, but harmonizes in tune with Kurosawa's version. [Full review in Spanishi]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: Gripping and cumulatively powerful cinematic fare...
reviews.author: Mark Demetrius

reviews.text: I can picture this version being used in high schools in coming years to come. Excellent
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: As great as the performances are, it's how they are aligned with the direction and staging that make The Tragedy of Macbeth a thoroughly exhilarating watch.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Coen presents a theatre-film hybrid; the old blends with the new by retaining traditionalist elements while reviving the visual to give audiences a new lens for this classic tale of tragedy.
reviews.author: Rachael Sampson

reviews.text: Coen's version of Macbeth is a canny, fascinating hybrid of a theatrical sensibility and a cinematic translation, shot in ghostly monochrome.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Phenomenally dark and wicked, Coen's The Tragedy of Macbeth is the most worthy adaptation of a Shakespearean work that has been seen on screen in years.
reviews.author: Aramide Tinubu

reviews.text: By choosing Washington and McDormand as his leads, Coen puts a fresh spin on familiar phrases.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Aesthetically striking and deeply disturbing...anchored by two powerhouses of the acting world, it is easy to get sucked into Coen's bold vision.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Stark but utterly compelling, this chilling take on Macbeth is a visually stunning tour de force. It's as good as you'd expect from this cast and crew, which is saying something.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: Denzel Washington, Frances McDormand and a solo Joel Coen turn Shakespeare's bloody classic into a ravishingly beautiful game of thrones.
reviews.author: Stephen Dalton

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is full of lovely, obvious, expressionistic style choices, which not only registered on my limited Shakespeare palate but felt invigorating after 18 months of watching mediocrely lensed historical dramas on my TV.
reviews.author: Violet Lucca

reviews.text: It's a really well-done adaptation.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Every frame of The Tragedy of Macbeth is a work of art. There is not so much as a hair on a head or a leaf on a tree that does not feel precisely curated.
reviews.author: Ciara Wardlow

reviews.text: There comes a point in every year when audiences see a film they believe is this year's masterpiece. This is that time, that film.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Washington and McDormand both seem to get better with each new screen performance. It's truly astonishing.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: This synthesis of cinematic and theatrical leans towards the latter, producing an exciting and fascinating merger of mediums.
reviews.author: Jonah Koslofsky

reviews.text: At best, The Tragedy of Macbeth feels like a vanity project where a director trying to please his wife a role she always wanted to play (for 15 years apparently). It also gives a clue to which Coen might be a Garfunkel of the duo.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: By keeping the essential components of Shakespeare's play and abstracting everything else, Joel Coen has not only honored one of the greatest pieces of literature of all time, but has created a wicked reimagining that casts a powerful spell.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: It is one of many Macbeth revivals shot since the first one in 1908, and is one of the really good ones.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Joel Coen's triumphant film of Shakespeare's tragedy astounds on every level, with Denzel Washington and Frances McDormand, two acting titans, playing an aging couple taking their last shot at murderous ambition. You can't take your eyes off them.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The best part of this impressive film is the below-the-line talent that Joel Coen assembled to create a minimalist but gripping rendition
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Anchored by a commanding, deeply layered performance by Denzel, "Macbeth" gives a unique visually stunning adaptation of the famous play. Despite some technical missteps, this is a creative triumph!
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: It's a story that you know and has been adapted through many mediums, but Coen, Washington, Mcdormand, Hunter, and a talented ensemble makes the play memorable again.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: With his singular manoeuvres of dark humours and romanticist aesthetics, Coen proves that a fundamental tragedy can be viscerally enjoyable.
reviews.author: Weiting Liu

reviews.text: It's stage-bound in all the right ways, reminiscent of a much earlier cinema, when filmmakers barely stepped outdoors and wielded magic with shadow and light on soundstages. It's short, sharp and savage.
reviews.author: Dave Calhoun

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is an old-man film, its reinterpretation of juvenile folly shot through with a visceral fear of aging and bodily disintegration
reviews.author: Patrick Preziosi

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth is visually spectacular. The cinematography is riveting, and certain shots will have your jaw on the floor. The story itself is not as engaging as the visuals, but Coen and his cast still manage impress on every level.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Move over, Branagh!
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: Macbeth becomes, like so many of the Coens' protagonists, a character trapped in his own fixations and failings, the concave world onscreen a reflection of the self he can't escape.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: For those who seek a safely satisfying rendition of the lean Shakespearean tragedy, this latest execution will surely suffice.
reviews.author: Natalia Keogan

reviews.text: There's real resonant power in all that sound and fury - a tragedy stripped back and reborn but the essential truth of it undiminished, half a millennium on.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Vivid proof that life still pumps through the doomed Scottish king's veins.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: Visceral, haunted and severe, Coen's vision coaxes out not just the intensity in the play - every "gritty" take has done this, from Roman Polanski to Justin Kurzel - but its older renderings too.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: Joel Coen's The Tragedy of Macbeth is austere in its presentation, yet is brimming with intensity. The stark black and white cinematography is something to behold.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: What Coen has achieved is magnificent and monumental, not words to be thrown around. He's exceeded his best past work and then some. This production is almost hybrid theater-cinema, using the best techniques of each.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: The Tragedy of Macbeth gives William Shakespeare's play Macbeth the minimalist treatment, laying bare the raw intensity of the story, which is masterfully channeled via powerhouse performances from Denzel Washington and Frances McDormand.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The film's true stars are Coen, cinematographer Bruno Delbonnel, and production designer Stefan Dechant. The look these three have created is magnificently bleak and sumptuously arid, a banquet of vapor.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: It captures age-old story beats with thrilling panache, answering the question of how you restage Macbeth for the umpteenth time, in 2021, with a resounding counter: you do it the way it's been done before, and you do it better.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The film's visuals, like the text, are a marvel, and hearken back to any number of German Expressionist classics.
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: It's an efficient little film, despite its fussy aesthetics... But it's veteran stage performer Kathryn Hunter, as all three of the Weird Sisters (or is there just one?), who conjures the play's horror most persuasively.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: A triumph that breathes fiery new life into an enduring classic.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: But it's also simply a hell of a film- dark, moody, inscrutable, yet also as accessible a representation of the Bard's florid language as one is likely to find.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: Furious and fleet, emotional and elemental, Joel Coen's stripped-down take on the Scottish play instantly secures its place among the most audacious modern screen adaptations of Shakespeare.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Nothing short of magnificent.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: Coen's compositions echo F.W. Murnau, Carl Dreyer, and other Expressionists, matching the artifice of the stage with cinema at its most beautifully artificial.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: The performance that best captured the joy and despair of the source material was Kathryn Hunter's, as she portrays all three weird sisters in one avian, contorting body.
reviews.author: Amelia Merrill

reviews.text: Denzel and McDormand are fearless, and "The Tragedy of Macbeth" is an enthralling jolt of verse and just good old-fashioned dread.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Coen's work in The Tragedy of Macbeth is otherworldly.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: Combines the sparseness of a late career work with the back-to-basics energy of a veteran filmmaker starting a new chapter of their career, and returning to the primordial ooze that inspired it in the first place.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: A bracingly textured cinematic plunge into some classically dark waters.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: It resonates with the ancient power of a ritual.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: A "Macbeth" that is sure to seduce audiences - one that, for all its darkness of import, is light-spirited, fleet, and intoxicating.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: This is a black-and-white world of violence and pain that scorches the retina.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

synopsis: Joel Coen's bold and fierce adaptation of "Macbeth," a tale of murder, madness, ambition, and wrathful cunning.
